drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Here is your opening scenario. A manufacturer runs on Microsoft
drills.answer_line: SAM: That is the core of it. The answer is C.
drills.stem: A Microsoft 365 Copilot customer is behind on a large Azure consumption commitment, and procurement will approve new AI spend only through the Azure bill. Engineering wants Claude for an internal agent over maintenance manuals, using the Messages API with tool calls. What do you advise?

options.A: Use Azure OpenAI instead: a Microsoft shop should stay on Microsoft's models
options.B: Sign directly with Anthropic for the newest features on day one
options.C: Deploy Claude through Microsoft Foundry, billed against the Azure commitment, after checking the needed features are supported
options.D: Microsoft 365 Copilot already includes Claude, so nothing more is needed

drills.why: The constraint picks the route: Foundry bills through Azure Marketplace against the Azure commitment, and Messages with tool calls is supported. Check for Managed Agents or batch needs and CSP purchasing. A misreads 'Microsoft shop'; B is a separate contract off the Azure bill; D confuses the enterprise wrapper with the developer platform.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A law firm rolled out ChatGPT Enterprise
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. It fits both stated facts
drills.stem: Partners use ChatGPT Enterprise daily. The forty engineers trialled Codex and Claude Code on their own repositories and prefer Claude Code. What should the CIO do?

options.A: Replace ChatGPT Enterprise with Claude across the firm, for consistency
options.B: Keep ChatGPT Enterprise, add Claude Code for engineers, govern both under one AI policy
options.C: Block ChatGPT and mandate Claude for everyone
options.D: Keep everyone on OpenAI, engineers on Codex, because one vendor is simpler

drills.why: Fits both facts: high chat adoption and the engineers' own trial. A and C spend adoption on tidiness; D overrides the engineers' evidence.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false.
drills.prompt: True or false? 1) Claude in Microsoft Foundry draws down an Azure consumption commitment. 2) Claude billed through AWS also draws down a Microsoft commitment. 3) Claude Managed Agents are available in Foundry. 4) OpenAI's models are GA on Amazon Bedrock. 5) An Azure subscription bought through a CSP partner can buy Claude in Foundry.
drills.answer: 1) True. 2) False. 3) False. 4) True. 5) False: CSP, free trial and credit-based subscriptions are excluded.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A media analytics firm on Google Cloud
drills.answer_line: SAM: C, and that bet is fair
drills.stem: A Google Cloud customer runs millions of short classification calls a day and a hard multi-step research agent. Finance says Gemini is cheaper, so move everything. What do you advise?

options.A: Move everything to Claude: quality on the agent matters most
options.B: Move everything to Gemini: price per token is lower
options.C: Eval each workload on their own data, compare cost per accepted result at post-promotion prices, accept different models per workload
options.D: Pick whichever model leads Arena's text board

drills.why: Two workloads, two answers possible; cost per accepted result at the price that will apply. A and B apply one workload's logic to both; D uses a human-preference board for jobs it does not measure.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A federal health contractor
drills.answer_line: SAM: That is choosing the richer route over the stated constraint.
drills.stem: A federal health contractor needs FedRAMP High and HIPAA coverage, runs on AWS, and has a GCC High Microsoft 365 tenant. It wants Claude to summarise case files. What fits?

options.A: Claude Platform on AWS, for the native API and same-day features
options.B: Claude on Amazon Bedrock, inside the AWS boundary, building the agent loop themselves
options.C: Claude inside their Microsoft 365 Copilot tenant
options.D: A DeepSeek-based fine-tune hosted in their own account

drills.why: Compliance belongs to the endpoint: Bedrock is the documented route for FedRAMP High and HIPAA. A is not HIPAA-ready and processes data outside the AWS boundary; C is not offered in GCC High; D is excluded by the DHS order.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A bank wants Claude, G P T and Gemini
drills.answer_line: SAM: A and C. B is the reverse problem
drills.stem: Choose two. A bank wants Claude, GPT and Gemini behind one gateway so it can switch models without rewriting applications. Which two practices fit?

options.A: Logical aliases mapped to pinned model versions per environment, eval before each swap
options.B: Point production at each vendor's 'latest' alias
options.C: Treat the gateway as tier-zero: pin versions, verify hashes, isolate its keys
options.D: Choose an open-source gateway because it cannot be compromised
options.E: Route every request to the cheapest model listed

drills.why: Aliases plus pinning make a swap a config change and an eval run; the gateway holds every key. B changes models without an eval, D is contradicted by the LiteLLM attack, E ignores the task.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A consumer brand on Google Cloud
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. It fits the platform they have
drills.stem: A consumer brand on Google Cloud wants an assistant that drafts campaign copy and produces short product videos with sound. What do you advise?

options.A: Claude for everything, generating video through code execution
options.B: Google's video model via Google Cloud, Claude or Gemini for copy per their eval, all billed to Google Cloud
options.C: Wait for Anthropic to release a video model
options.D: A self-hosted open-weight pipeline to avoid any vendor

drills.why: Claude has no first-party video model; Google leads text-to-video. A stretches a tool, C sells an unpublished roadmap, D adds GPU operations with no requirement for them.

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the ten objections
drills.prompt: Name the ten objections, and the question you ask back for each.
drills.answer: Microsoft shop: which layer? Commitment elsewhere: which features? ChatGPT: personal or company plan? Gemini cheaper, Claude expensive: per token or per result? Benchmark: whose, at what cost? Self-host: what must stay where? Lock-in: where is the state? FedRAMP or HIPAA: which endpoint? Image or video: not Claude.

In this episode: Estate objections: Microsoft, cloud commitment, ChatGPT
Money objections: Gemini cheaper, Claude expensive, benchmarks
Control objections: self-hosting, lock-in, FedRAMP and HIPAA
Cold open: the Azure-committed manufactu: Microsoft 365 with Copilot already in place
Behind on an Azure consumption commitment
New AI spend only through the Azure bill
Agent on the Messages API with tool calls
Segment one: what the customer already o: Claude in Microsoft 365 Copilot: Anthropic is a Microsoft subprocessor
Copilot Cowork runs on named Anthropic models; GPT in Frontier
'Cheaper per prompt' claim is Microsoft's own test: vendor-reported
OpenAI on Bedrock, Claude in Foundry: commitment no longer picks the lab
Features differ by route: Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Foundry
Stack Overflow 2026: Claude Code 66%, GitHub Copilot 59% of AI users
Segment two: price and proof: Ranks as of November 2026; episode eight holds the numbers
Gemini: intro prices ending, implicit caching only, fast Flash churn
Google strong on intelligence per dollar; OpenAI's Sol on cost per task
Cache reads can be 95%+ of agent tokens (Menlo, an Anthropic investor)
No one leads every board; cite independent ones that fit the job
SWE-bench Verified and Pro lost OpenAI's endorsement in 2026
Segment three: control: Self-host: weights, data, operator access, or jurisdiction?
Open weights: Gemma 4 Apache 2.0, Mistral EU inference; licence drift
Lock-in lives in stateful managed services and platform churn
MCP under the Linux Foundation's AAIF; Claude Code reads AGENTS.md
Gateways are tier-zero: LiteLLM attack, Portkey and OpenRouter sold
Compliance belongs to the endpoint, not the logo
Segment four: when the answer is not Cla: No first-party image, video, music, speech or embedding models
Google leads text-to-video; OpenAI leads text-to-image
Realtime voice: OpenAI and Google, not Anthropic
Hold the line on agentic coding and long-running agents
Cold open: the verdict: Answer: C, Claude through Microsoft Foundry
Foundry billing counts against the Azure commitment
Check: no Managed Agents or batch API on Foundry
Check: CSP-bought Azure cannot buy Claude
Tell: 'only through the Azure bill', 'behind on the commitment'
Five to remember: Microsoft shop and commitments are route to market: match features
Price is cost per accepted result: caching, routing, post-promo price
No one leads every benchmark: independent, job-shaped, your own tasks
Compliance belongs to the endpoint: FedRAMP and HIPAA point to Bedrock
Recommend competitors for media, voice, open weights; keep the exit open
Recap: the conversation tells: 'Microsoft shop' → is Claude already on in your tenant?
'Our money is on AWS' → which features? Bedrock or Claude Platform on AWS
'Staff use ChatGPT' → governed rollout? Then leave it
'Gemini is cheaper' or 'a benchmark says' → cost per result on your tasks
'We must self-host' → weights, data, operators or jurisdiction?
'No lock-in' → aliases, pinned versions, your own evals
'FedRAMP or HIPAA' → which endpoint holds the authorisation?
'We need video or voice' → recommend the competitor
